title: Vtree2 User Guide
text: vtree2, workflow split several steps: Prepare data (outside vtree2) Build vtree object vtree() vtree_from_freqtable() (Optional) Prune, retain select nodes prune(), retain() friends. (Optional) Create summaries summarize_by_node() fmt_label(). (Optional) Add aliases variable names values add_aliases(). (Optional) Add modify labels add_labels() mutate(). (Optional) Add modify colors add_palette() mutate(). Plot vtree plot(). example demonstrating steps based titanicNA data set. data set Titanic data set, missing values randomly added demonstration purposes.
code: data(titanicNA)  vtree(titanicNA, Class, Sex, Survived) |>   # only retain the third class passengers   retain(path == "Class:3rd") |>   # change how variables are displayed   add_aliases(val_alias = list(Class = c("1st" = "First",                                     "2nd" = "Second",                                     "3rd" = "Third"))) |>   # add default labels, built from aliases   add_labels() |>   # change the labels for the missing values   mutate(label = gsub("NA", "Missing", label)) |>   # add colors   add_palette(palettes = c("Greys", "Blues", "Purples"),               na = "grey90") |>   # change the color for Females who survived   # mark() adds a column `mark` to the vtree object, which is TRUE for   # nodes that match the given condition   mark(path == "Class:3rd/Sex:Female/Survived:Yes") |>   mutate(fill = ifelse(mark, "red", fill)) |>   mutate(color = ifelse(mark, "white", color)) |>   mutate(label = ifelse(mark, sprintf("**%s**", label), label)) |>   # plotting with legend and custom margins   plot(legend = TRUE,        richtext = TRUE,        margins = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.25, 0.05))

Default “lr”.  fontsizes Font sizes various labels automatically fit available space, sometimes might manually adjust . fontsizes named list following optional fields: * nodes: node labels (default: “fixed” regular layout, “adaptive” proportional layout) * var_labels: variable labels (default: “fixed”) * legend_labels: variable levels legend=TRUE (default: “fixed”) element can either number, case given font size directly used, either “fixed” “adaptive”. “fixed” used, optimal font size calculated objects within group, minimal font size used objects. “adaptive” used, object fit separately, font sizes can different object. padding: can try tweak parameter padding label nodes legend liking. vtree2 attempts dynamically fit text inside nodes, always works. parameter interpreted desired fraction width/height label used padding, effective padding depends actual device size geometry. lwd line width use plotting. code: dessert <- vtree::build.data.frame(   c(   "group","IceCream___1","IceCream___2","IceCream___3"),   list("A",     1,             0,             0,              7),   list("A",     1,             0,             1,              2),   list("A",     0,             0,             0,              1),   list("A",     1,             1,             1,              1),   list("B",     1,             0,             1,              1),   list("B",     1,             0,             0,              2),    list("B",     0,             1,             1,              1),   list("B",     0,             0,             0,              1)) attr(dessert$IceCream___1,"label") <- "Ice cream (choice=Chocolate)" attr(dessert$IceCream___2,"label") <- "Ice cream (choice=Vanilla)" attr(dessert$IceCream___3,"label") <- "Ice cream (choice=Strawberry)" rewrite_redcap <- function(df, ident) {   cols <- startsWith(colnames(df), ident)   fnc <- \(x) {     nn <- attr(df[[x]], "label")     pat <- ".* \\(choice=(.*)\\)"     nn <- gsub(pat, "\\1", nn)     nn   }   newnames <- vapply(colnames(df)[cols], fnc, character(1))   colnames(df)[cols] <- newnames   df }  rewrite_redcap(dessert, "IceCream___") |>   mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) |>   vtree(Chocolate, Vanilla, Strawberry) |>   plot()

title: What are vtrees?
text: main purpose vtrees understand visualize hierarchical, categorical data. vtree tree diagram shows data split levels categorical variables. example frequently used vtree package, Titanic data set, several categorical variables, Class (passenger class), Sex (gender) Survived (whether passenger survived sinking Titanic). may ask, example, many female passengers traveling first class survived? percentage among first class female passengers? Rather calculating numbers manually, can visualize one go vtree:  follow path root node left, first class, female passengers, survivors, notice percentage survivors among first class calculated :  way, reminding consort diagram. can style plot looks bit like consort diagram:
code: cases <- cases_from_freqtable(Titanic) head(cases) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   Class Sex   Age   Survived #>   <fct> <fct> <fct> <fct>    #> 1 3rd   Male  Child No       #> 2 3rd   Male  Child No       #> 3 3rd   Male  Child No       #> 4 3rd   Male  Child No       #> 5 3rd   Male  Child No       #> 6 3rd   Male  Child No  # female 1st class survivors sum(cases$Class == "1st" & cases$Sex == "Female" & cases$Survived == "Yes") #> [1] 141  # percentage sum(cases$Class == "1st" & cases$Sex == "Female" & cases$Survived == "Yes") /   sum(cases$Class == "1st" & cases$Sex == "Female") * 100 #> [1] 97.24138 vt <- vtree(cases, Class, Sex, Survived)  plot(vt) vt |>   mark(path %in% c("root", "Class:1st", "Class:1st/Sex:Female",                    "Class:1st/Sex:Female/Survived:Yes")) |>   mutate(fill = ifelse(mark, "red", "white")) |>   plot() #> ℹ palette attribute is NULL #> legend will be black and white vt |>   mutate(fill = "white") |>   plot(dir="tb", layout="flushed_right", legend = FALSE)

title: What are vtrees?
text: following example may convince use vtree representation can data. Imagine disease test disease. good test? can consider often test makes error infected subject, incorrectly giving negative result. called false negative (FN). probability error called false negative rate (FNR), compliment sensitivity: sensitive test , less likely test result negative person sick. Let’s assume test highly sensitive, example FNR 2% (making sensitivity 98%). Another type error healthy subject, test showing positive. value number false positives (FP) divided total number healthy people, also known FPR - false positive rate. complement value (1−FPR1 - FPR) called specificity. Say, outstanding test specificity 98%, false positive rate 2%. OK, story. Whether positive test result corresponds real patient false positive depends likely person actually healthy reality. disease prevalence, often disease encountered people tested. Say, disease quite common, prevalence 2%. , assuming performed screening tests 5^{4} persons population, get following table: can build data: can visualize table vtree. Since frequency table, need use vtree_from_freqtable() function1. starters, show Status first, Test result. show us many healthy persons incorrectly classified positive, many infected persons incorrectly classified negative.  can see, percentages leaf nodes (right side plot) correspond FPR FNR values. percentages internal nodes correspond disease prevalence. inverse question? fraction healthy people among tested positive, vice versa - fraction infected people among tested negative?  see among tested negative, large majority (practically 100%) indeed healthy. negative predictive value (NPV) test. However, among tested positive, 50% actually infected. positive predictive value (PPV) test shows despite test specific sensitive, person positive test result, 50% chance person actually healthy.
code: FPR <- .02 # p that healthy is positive FNR <- .02 # p that infected is negative prevalence <- 1/50  N <- 50000  data <- tribble(  ~ Status, ~ Test, ~ N,  "Infected", "Positive", round(prevalence * N * (1-FNR)),  "Infected", "Negative", round(prevalence * N * FNR),  "Healthy",  "Positive", round((1 - prevalence) * N * FNR),   "Healthy",  "Negative", round((1 - prevalence) * N * (1 - FNR))  ) vt <- vtree_from_freqtable(data,                            Status, Test,                            .freq_col = "N") plot(vt) vt2 <- vtree_from_freqtable(data,                            Test, Status,                            .freq_col = "N") plot(vt2)

Likewise, missing total number persons 1st class know whether male female. denom variable depend .vp. need valid percentages (default), denom equal tot_n - missing; otherwise tot_n. tot_n information redundant, since can read directly n parent node (Class:1st case Class:1st/Sex:Female).
